2021_02_memo_re_bloomfield_proposed_agre.page:
**What it is**
A memorandum from the law firm Collins & Blaha, P.C., dated January 26, 2021, addressed to the International Academy (IA) Governing Body c/o Dr. Richard M. Machesky, Superintendent, Troy School District, authored by Gary J. Collins, Esq. and John C. Kava, Esq., on the subject "Requested Consortium Agreement Amendments." It was included in the Troy Board of Education packet for February 23, 2021.

**Background**
Bloomfield Hills Schools sent a proposed International Academy Consortium Agreement Amendment to the Governing Body on November 24, 2020. Bloomfield's Board of Education did not approve the Consortium Agreement that the other IA districts approved in the summer of 2020, but Bloomfield has continued to participate in the IA Consortium. Bloomfield had earlier raised concerns about the 2020 Agreement's governance structure and other provisions, including employment of the principal. Counsel report that the latest proposal omits most of those earlier issues and focuses on clean-up and clarification, and that the amendments can be agreed upon so the Consortium can move forward with all current member districts.

**The six substantive amendments described**
1. Clarify in the definition of "Academy" that the Consortium operates at more than one campus.
2. Amend Article III, Section 3(A) on admission of new participants so that, in addition to Governing Body approval, the Superintendent of the Fiscal Agent for the campus the new participant will attend must vote in the affirmative; the approval must also specify the number of Shares allotted.
3. Amend Article IV, Section 1(B)(1) to list overhead costs the Governing Body may allocate to each campus, including IB license fees, legal fees and expenses, and the cost of employing the Principal and other administrators shared by all three campuses, including salaries, benefits, and insurance premiums.
4. Amend Article IV, Section 1(C) to remove the reference to a Superintendent's "designee," so that Superintendents themselves must act.
5. Amend Article IV, Section 1(G)(3) so that discipline resulting in a suspension longer than ten days must be referred to the student's district of residence, which provides due process.
6. Update the Appendices, including the list of Consortium participants and the billing and payment provisions of Appendix B, which counsel say business managers should review.

**Exhibit A — redlined First Amendment**
The draft First Amendment to the Amended and Restated International Academy Consortium Agreement names Bloomfield Hills Schools, Troy School District, and Huron Valley Schools as Fiscal Agents, and Appendix D assigns IA OKMA Campus to Bloomfield Hills Schools, IA West to Huron Valley School District, and IA East to Troy School District. It restates paragraphs in Articles II, III, IV and VI, requires all blanks and Appendices A, B and C to be completed before execution, and provides that the First Amendment controls in the event of conflict with the Agreement.

**Exhibit B — model resolution**
A blank resolution for each Participating District's board, reciting that a majority of IA Participating School Districts approved an amended governance structure and Consortium Agreement effective July 1, 2020, that Section X, Paragraph 5 permits amendment by written instrument executed by a majority of the Participating districts, approving the amended Agreement and authorizing the District's Superintendent to execute it, with an Open Meetings Act (Act 267, Public Acts of 1976) certification.

A memorandum on the letterhead of COLLINS & BLAHA, P.C., dated January 26, 2021, from Gary J. Collins, Esq. and John C. Kava, Esq. to the International Academy Governing Body, c/o Dr. Richard M. Machesky, Superintendent, Troy School District, captioned "Re: Requested Consortium Agreement Amendments." The memo, with two attached exhibits, was carried in the Troy School District Board of Education packet for the February 23, 2021 meeting. Document control numbers appearing in the filing include 4819-1377-8905 v. 1 (the memorandum and Exhibit B cover), 4850-6138-0821 v. 1 and 21974\390020\261132652.v2 (Exhibit A), and 4830-5626-7993 v. 1 (Exhibit B resolution).

BACKGROUND. Bloomfield Hills Schools ("Bloomfield") sent a proposed International Academy Consortium Agreement Amendment to the Governing Body on November 24, 2020. Counsel reviewed the proposal and discussed it with Bloomfield's legal counsel, and it is counsel's understanding that Governing Body members had the opportunity to speak with the Participating School Districts' superintendents to explain the request. The memorandum is framed as an update that the Governing Body can share with the Consortium Participating Districts; Exhibit A is a redlined version of the proposed amendment and Exhibit B is a draft resolution each Participating School District may use for board approval. Bloomfield's Board of Education did not approve the Consortium Agreement that the other IA school districts approved in the summer of 2020, but Bloomfield has continued to participate in the IA Consortium. Bloomfield had previously raised concerns with the governance structure of the 2020 Consortium Agreement and several other provisions, including employment of the principal. Counsel state that the latest proposal does not include many of those previously raised issues and instead focuses on clean-up and clarification, and that the amendments are items the IA Consortium members can agree upon so the Consortium can move forward with all districts currently in it.

THE SIX SUBSTANTIVE AMENDMENTS SUMMARIZED IN THE MEMO. (1) Clarify in the definition of "Academy" that the Consortium operates at more than one campus. (2) Amend the admission-of-new-participants paragraph, Article III, Section 3(A), so that in addition to Governing Body approval, the Superintendent of the Fiscal Agent for the campus at which the new participant will be located must vote in the affirmative for the Governing Body's action to be effective, and so that approval specifies the number of Shares allotted to the new participant. (3) Amend Article IV, Section 1(B)(1), on the Governing Body's powers, to include a more detailed list of overhead costs the Governing Body can allocate to each campus, including IB license fees, legal fees and expenses, and costs to employ the Principal and other administrators shared by all three campuses, including salaries, benefits, and insurance premiums. (4) Amend Article IV, Section 1(C) to remove the reference to the Superintendent's "designee," the substance being that Superintendents must be the individuals to act rather than designees who do not regularly attend meetings. (5) Amend Article IV, Section 1(G)(3) to state clearly that disciplinary action resulting in a suspension longer than ten days must be referred to the student's district of residence, which shall provide due process. (6) A statement that the Appendices must be updated, including the list of IA Consortium participants and the operation of payments and billing under Appendix B, with counsel advising that business managers review Appendix B.

EXHIBIT A — FIRST AMENDMENT TO AMENDED AND RESTATED INTERNATIONAL ACADEMY CONSORTIUM AGREEMENT. The redlined instrument is drafted to be entered into as of a blank Effective Date in 2020 and attached to the Amended and Restated Agreement, between and among the Boards of Education of the school districts listed in Appendix A. Recitals note the Amended and Restated Agreement was ratified by a blank number of school districts and that additional districts desire to ratify with the First Amendment's modifications. Amended and restated provisions include: Article II Definitions Paragraph A, "ACADEMY" — the International Academy operated by the Consortium at one or more Campuses; Article II Definitions Paragraph G, "FISCAL AGENT" — Bloomfield Hills Schools District, Troy School District, and Huron Valley Schools serve as Fiscal Agents for all Consortium Programming and services at their respective Campuses per Appendix D; Article III, Section 3(A) Admission of New Participants — a Michigan school district may be admitted by Governing Body action, but the Superintendent of the Fiscal Agent for the Campus the new Participating District intends to send its students must vote affirmatively for that action to be effective, the decision must then be ratified by a majority of the Participating Districts, and the approval must specify the number of Shares and the Campus, with the new district contributing to operating, capital outlay and start-up costs on a pro-rata basis depending on Shares and admission date; Article III, Section 3(B) Limited Effects of Withdrawal — no resignation or withdrawal by a Participant or Fiscal Agent annuls the Agreement, terminates the Consortium, or relieves the withdrawing party of its obligations unless all Participants agree otherwise.

Article IV, Section 1(B)(1), fifth paragraph, limits the Governing Body's powers to: (i) allocation of Consortium overhead expenses to each Campus Program, including dues and fees payable to the International Baccalaureate organization including the cost of the IB license, administrative expenses incurred on behalf of all three Campus Programs, other expenses incurred on behalf of more than one Campus Program including legal fees and expenses for legal advice or representation, and costs of employing the Academy's Principal, Coordinator(s) or other administrators shared by all three Campuses including salaries, benefits and liability/professional insurance premiums; (ii) monitoring and ensuring compliance with IB standards and certification requirements; (iii) management of the process of electing at-large members to the Governing Body; (iv) oversight of the withdrawal and dissolution processes; and (v) any other express power granted in the Agreement, with all other powers exercised by the Fiscal Agents. Article IV, Section 1(C) names Bloomfield Hills Schools, Troy School District, and Huron Valley Schools as the Consortium's Fiscal Agents, each Fiscal Agent's board adopting a resolution appointing its Superintendent as District representative; Bloomfield Hills Schools serves the OKMA Campus, Troy School District the Troy East Campus, and Huron Valley Schools the West Campus.

Article IV, Section 1(G)(3) Discipline provides that each Campus shall have a Student Code of Conduct set by its Fiscal Agent; students are subject to the Campus's code while in attendance; the building principal or other designated administrator of that Campus may discipline students; where a disciplinary action results in suspension from school for more than ten (10) days the building principal shall advise the student's district of residence, which shall provide due process and take appropriate action; and the Fiscal Agent for the Campus retains authority to exclude a student from its Campus, after which the student's School District of residence determines the admittance, suspension, or expulsion process. Article VI, Section 2 provides that the Academy Principal shall be employed by one of the Fiscal Agents, shall be the Academy Principal for all Consortium Campuses, and shall be evaluated by the employing Fiscal Agent, which may seek evaluation input from the other Fiscal Agents; the job description is approved and may be modified by the employing Fiscal Agent with input from the others.

Housekeeping items in Exhibit A: signature lines must be updated to refer only to school districts that authorized the amendment by board resolution before execution; Appendix A's "[UPDATE MEMBER DISTRICTS]" reference must be replaced with the actual list of Participating Districts; Appendix B must state that the Consortium and each Campus operate under the Uniform Budgeting and Accounting Act, Public Act No. 2 of 1968, the State School Aid Act and other state financial laws, and counsel flag that the billing and payment schedule cross-reference is defective — Appendix B cites Article IV, Section 3, which concerns Transfer of Shares, while counsel believe the proper citations may be Article II, Section 2(A)(2) and Article V, Section 1(E), the latter applying only to the OKMA Campus, and further note it is unclear what start-up costs mean for a Consortium that has been running for years; Appendix C-3 blanks must be filled in and the Letters of Agreement referenced in Appendix C, Article VI, Section 1(D) must actually be attached. Appendix D sets the Campus/Fiscal Agent pairs: IA OKMA Campus — Bloomfield Hills Schools; IA West — Huron Valley School District; IA East — Troy School District. Section B ratifies and reaffirms the Agreement except as modified, with the First Amendment controlling in the event of conflict.

EXHIBIT B — MODEL BOARD RESOLUTION. A fill-in-the-blank "Resolution Regarding International Academy Agreement" for a named school district and county in the State of Michigan, to be adopted at a regular meeting in 2021, with blanks for the presiding officer, members present and absent, and the mover and supporter. Recitals state that the District is a Participating District in the International Academy and a party to the Consortium Agreement; that a majority of IA Participating School Districts approved an amended governance structure and Consortium Agreement effective July 1, 2020; that the Governing Body received a proposed amendment from a Participating School District, reviewed it, consulted legal counsel, and circulated it with a memo; that Section X, Paragraph 5 of the Consortium Agreement permits amendment only by written instrument executed by a majority of the Participating districts; and that the Board deems approval in the District's best interests. The resolution approves the proposed Amended Consortium Agreement attached as Exhibit A, authorizes the District's Superintendent to execute it, and rescinds conflicting resolutions. A secretary's certification follows, attesting compliance with the Open Meetings Act, being Act 267, Public Acts of 1976.

Read together, the amendments reflect a pandemic-year reshaping of the district's non-general funds: local revenue collapses in the Food Service, Community Service, Preschool and Facility Rentals funds, offset in part by large increases in federal food-service reimbursement and new state preschool revenue; the Community Service and Preschool funds pick up incoming transfers; construction spending accelerates in the 2019 Capital Projects Fund while the Sinking Fund's facilities acquisition budget is cut sharply and a debt service line is added; and the Early Childhood Learning Center Capital Projects Fund receives its first budget, fully drawing down its beginning balance.
